purpose.summary: Add a fail-closed local harness for the final assembled optional-indexing boundary without promoting local observation to public reproduction.
scope: Fetch public main over bounded HTTPS, then verify an exact signed single-parent candidate, its direct signed integration parent, the signed parentless public root, and the complete clean source history without lazy object fetching.

Reject assume-unchanged and skip-worktree index flags, verify the governed harness and record against the signed tree, and give every build role its own exact raw-byte materialization from an isolated read-tree/checkout-index index rather than the checkout or an attribute-filtered archive.

Create three fresh out-of-source build graphs with C/C++ caching disabled for compiled-out, build-only Rust foundations, and the compiled-in observer; verify every registry archive against Cargo.lock, exclude pre-extracted sources, bind the copied index and archives by manifest, and use separate offline Cargo homes.

Require the harness itself to enter through Python isolated mode, then run inherited mining with the observer compiled out and compiled in but runtime disabled, focused Rust units, and the six bounded local-regtest observer scenarios with functional-child user sites disabled while signed-tree sibling imports remain available.

Require isolated test state, bounded jobs and timeouts, enforced Git/signature output-file limits, process-group cleanup, unchanged source and binary identities, and a strict privacy-preserving JSON receipt.
Preserve compile-time default OFF, runtime default OFF, explicit local-regtest-only opt-in, and observe/index-only operation.
exclusions: No consensus, validation, mempool, chain-selection, activation, chain-parameter, testnet, mainnet, P2P, RPC, wallet, user-interface, Chronik production, or functional-test behavior changes.

No workflow, container, toolchain image, dependency lock, cache publication, or public execution is added by this change; Cargo is locked and offline so no external build dependency is fetched, while functional nodes may use their required isolated loopback transport.
No claim of deterministic build, public reproduction, mainnet or testnet behavior, native-asset validity, persistence, stable API, or reproduction of every historical intermediate commit.
No absolute host path, parent environment, raw child output, cache, datadir, process data, private history, operator material, or unrelated product material enters the receipt or repository.

files.test_reachability: Governs exact public identities, three fresh build graphs, locked offline Rust checks, inherited mining, six optional-observer scenarios, cleanup, and receipt privacy.

commands: From an exact signed-tree materialization verified path-by-path by mode, blob, and raw bytes, configure a fresh graph with both Chronik options and the outer and native-sub-build C/C++ caches disabled, build bitcoind, require no observer symbol or Cargo edge, and run mining_basic.py under Python user-site isolation.
expected_results: No Chronik build edge or observer symbol enters bitcoind and inherited mining succeeds.

commands: From a separate exact signed-tree materialization, configure a fresh graph with BUILD_CHRONIK_OBSERVER=ON and outer/native C/C++ caching disabled, build bitcoind from its separately authenticated offline Cargo home, omit -chronikobserver, and run mining_basic.py under Python user-site isolation.
expected_results: The observer symbol is linked but the runtime-default-disabled node preserves inherited mining behavior.

commands: Reuse the exact compiled-in-disabled bitcoind, run check-chronik-observer, and execute the block, asset, and pruned observer functional tests on isolated fresh state.
expected_results: The exact same observer binary passes focused Rust units and all six bounded local-regtest reconstruction scenarios.

scenarios.command: Explicitly opt the compiled-in observer into isolated regtest and exercise confirmed-block connection, disconnection, and reconsideration.
expected_results: The worker-backed observer matches independent commitments without changing the node-authoritative tip.
failure_conditions: Non-regtest activation, missing linkage, commitment mismatch, state mutation on rejection, or validation influence fails the scenario.

scenarios.command: Restart explicit observer opt-in after building a retained active-chain suffix.
expected_results: Startup reconstructs and atomically adopts the exact ordered last-288-block projection.
failure_conditions: Partial adoption, stale state, wrong ordering, wrong commitment, worker loss, or growth beyond 288 blocks fails the scenario.

scenarios.command: Run a fresh full reindex process at height 288.
expected_results: Ordered block-file callbacks rebuild the exact bounded projection through the single owner.
failure_conditions: Missing, duplicated, reordered, rejected, or mismatched reconstructed observations fail the scenario.

scenarios.command: Run a fresh chainstate reindex process at height 288.
expected_results: Ordered chainstate callbacks rebuild the exact bounded projection without changing the active tip or UTXO-set hash.
failure_conditions: Bootstrap masking, block-file reindex, changed chain state, callback divergence, or mismatched records fail the scenario.

scenarios.command: Restart explicit observer opt-in on a fresh physically pruned height-1001 regtest datadir.
expected_results: The still-readable 288-block suffix reconstructs and the next connection preserves the bound.
failure_conditions: Skipped pruning, missing physical deletion, unreadable retained bodies, wrong suffix, event minting, record mismatch, or bound growth fails the scenario.

scenarios.command: Disconnect through the retained anchor, reject continuation, and restart for reconstruction.
expected_results: Records roll back LIFO, the single owner fails closed beyond its anchor, and restart reconstructs the active suffix.
failure_conditions: Non-LIFO acceptance, mutation after rebuild-required, unbounded retention, worker divergence, or node consensus influence fails the scenario.

platforms: Ubuntu 22.04 ARM64 public verification after technical acceptance

limitations: This change defines a local harness but does not execute it publicly or lock a public runner image and toolchain; its bounded Git fetch proves the candidate is public at execution time, not that the host toolchain is reproducible.
A passing local run can raise the final assembled optional observer only to Observed; it cannot establish Reproduced.
The final assembled candidate does not separately reproduce every historical intermediate identity from ERGON-CHANGE-0026 through ERGON-CHANGE-0032.
The build-only Rust graph is a supplemental foundation check and is not a fourth optional-indexing evidence role.
The pruning canary is bounded but consumes roughly 250 MiB of temporary disk and may take substantially longer than the other scenarios.
No deterministic-build, persistence, public-network, native-asset-validity, or stable-API conclusion follows from this harness.
counterevidence: No public execution receipt for the exact signed candidate exists at record-review time.
The existing public publication workflow validates governance files but does not build or execute the Chronik boundary.

A non-isolated main Python entry, pre-existing build, hidden checkout flag, attribute-filtered or incomplete source materialization, per-role signed-tree path/mode/blob/raw-byte mismatch or mutation, Cargo cache alias, altered locked crate archive, functional-child Python user customization, datadir alias, skipped test, changed binary, surviving process group, Git/signature output above the enforced file limit, nonzero child result, merge candidate, missing Git object, or isolated public-fetch mismatch invalidates the run.
Only a later locked public container or workflow plus an independent exact-candidate execution can support a Reproduced classification.
Chronik remains absent or disabled by default and never acquires consensus, mempool, activation, or chain-selection authority.
